\title{Correctness-Gated Policy Optimization for High-Frequency DSP
Accelerator RTL}

\author{Mohamed Amine Hallam%
\thanks{Mohamed Amine Hallam is with Harbin Institute of Technology,

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Functionally equivalent register-transfer-level (RTL) modules can differ
sharply in achievable clock frequency.  We train an RTL generator with a
correctness-gated physical objective: an input/output-equivalence oracle rejects
incorrect modules before a learned frequency proxy supplies reward.  The proxy
guides training but never supplies an evaluation result.  Instead, evaluation
joins original sample multiplicities to real post-route Vivado measurements and
assigns zero frequency to incorrect and implementation-failed samples.  In a
separately frozen \studyclaim{StudyTwoDesignCount}-design study, two independent
policy-training seeds using a random-forest physical reward raise the primary
equal-sample endpoint from \studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallSftPenalized} to
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfPenalized}~MHz, a
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftGain}-MHz paired gain with interval
[\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftCiLow},
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftCiHigh}]~MHz.  The combined policy remains close
in correctness to SFT and directly exceeds a matched multilayer-perceptron
reward by \studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfMlpGain}~MHz.  Conditional physical-cost
analysis shows more LUTs and registers, fewer DSP blocks, and a small vectorless
power increase.  A provenance-bound PYNQ-Z2 study provides heterogeneous
descriptive support: \boardclaim{BoardRfWins} RF wins,
\boardclaim{BoardTies} ties, and \boardclaim{BoardRfLosses} loss over
\boardclaim{BoardRunCount} sweeps with \boardclaim{BoardMaximumSpread}~MHz
maximum Fmax spread.  A bounded older
trajectory illustrates late reward overoptimization without displacing the
sealed result.  The proxy may guide training, but executable correctness, real
EDA, and disclosed silicon measurements remain the reporting authorities.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
RTL generation, reinforcement learning, large language models, FPGA,
design space exploration, reward hacking
\end{IEEEkeywords}
